scope: CPU fallback for caller-owned reserved virtual memory. The guest checks the three static imports and their package name/ordinal pairs. It requests two 64 KiB pages with the title's flags 0x20400000.
checks: Allocate distinct tokens into a guarded array. Map the pages into the middle of a four-page reservation. Write different patterns across all 131072 bytes.
Unmap using a null token array. Confirm the range returns to MEM_RESERVE. Remap the tokens in reverse order at a different base and verify every byte.

Reject a free while mapped, duplicate or unknown tokens, unaligned mapping, unsupported allocation flags and a stale token. Reject an unmap covering a foreign range and preserve a separate committed page.
Unmap and free individually, verify the neighboring live mapping remains committed, and release the full reservation.
implementation: The provider tracks tokens and mappings within each process. It backs live mappings with committed desktop virtual pages and retains their bytes in process memory while unmapped.
limitations: Both packaged DLL runs stopped during dependency initialization, before the guest could allocate pages. The control supplies no success-path output, Xbox error-code comparison or CPU byte comparison.
The fallback supports one live mapping per token and only the measured flag word. Copying contents during unmap and remap has a cost; large title workloads have not been benchmarked.
Xbox physical partitions, simultaneous alias mappings, GPU/DirectStorage access and retail use remain unverified.

reproduce.provider: python build.py xmem && python tuxbox.py verify --only xmem --output build/xmem-result.json
reproduce.package_control: Copy build/xmem-smoke/xmem-smoke.exe and the package xmem.dll, xbthunk.dll and xcrdapi.dll into an isolated directory. Run the guest with --pages --report result.txt on the selected Proton build with PROTON_LOG=1.
